rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A form used as an established noun or adjective is declinable; حطم illustrates the adjective class, with poetic evidence from al-Huṭam al-Qaysī.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن كل فعل كان اسما معروفا في الكلام أو صفة فهو مصروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These forms decline because they do not resemble augmented verbs, verbs without a nominal counterpart, or forms with a feminine ending.
rows.anchor: الذي في أوله زيادة وليست في آخره زيادة تأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar and Zafar are diptotes because they depart from their original patterns, ʿĀmir and Zāfir; such forms occur as definite names.
rows.anchor: وأما عمر وزفر فإنما منعهم من صرفهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh, following al-Khalil, says Umar declines when indefinite or diminutive because it no longer matches the altered proper-name pattern.
rows.anchor: صرفته لأنه نكرة فتحول عن موضع عامر معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zuhal is diptote when used as the name of the planet.
rows.anchor: وزحل معدول في حالة إذا أردت اسم الكوكب فلا ينصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamʿ and Kutaʿ are definite forms altered from Jamʿāʾ and Kutaʿāʾ, but they decline when indefinite.
rows.anchor: فقال هما معرفة بمنزلة كلهم وهما معدولتان عن جمع جمعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣughr as a proper name declines because it resembles Thuquba and is not altered from its expected pattern.
rows.anchor: وسألته عن صغر من قوله الصغري وصغر فقال أصرف هذا في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḫar is diptote in definite and indefinite use because it is an irregular adjective modeled on al-ṭūl, al-wasaṭ, and al-kibar.
rows.anchor: لا ينصرف في معرفة ولا نكرة فقال لأن أخر خالفت أخواتها وأصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vocative forms such as فسق are diptote by analogy with an understood vocative, while a diminutive proper name أخر becomes declinable.
rows.anchor: فلما خالفت الأصل وجاءت صفة بغير الألف واللام تركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr analyzes aḥād, thanā, mathnā, thulāth, and rubāʿ as diptote distributives meaning one by one, two by two, and so on; the Qur'anic phrase and Saʿida's poetry support him.
rows.anchor: أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These distributive forms remain diptote when indefinite because they themselves modify an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: قلت أفتصرفه في النكرة قال لا لأنه نكرة يوصف به نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diminutives of thanā and aḥād decline because diminutive formation removes the altered pattern that caused diptosis.
rows.anchor: ثناء وأحاد صرفته كما صرفت أخيرا وعميرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāl and Qīl as names decline because they are contracted verb forms in the speech of Tamīm, not names coined by alteration like Umar.
rows.anchor: أنك خففت فعل وفعل نفسه كما خففت الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar is not a deletion from ʿĀmir, just as mathnā is not clipped from ithnayn; it is a name built on an altered pattern.
rows.anchor: ولكنه اسم بني من هذا اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name such as Ḍarb becomes declinable when vowel reduction moves it into a regular declinable noun pattern; this is like diminutive formation.
rows.anchor: ثم خففته فأسكنت الراء صرفته لأنك قد أخرجته إلى مثال ما ينصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened name Hār shows why these reduced forms cannot be left diptote merely on the basis of alteration: Hār is clipped from hāʾir.
rows.anchor: صرف هذه الأشياء في التخفيف للعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ليس غير and ليس إلا, an understood complement such as ذاك is omitted for brevity because the listener can recover it.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال ليس إلا ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may omit an understood الواحد after من; Sibawayh adduces ordinary speech, Qur'an 4:159, and poetry as parallels.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك قوله تعالى جده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited poetry, expressions like من جمال and ما في قومها omit جمل and أحد, with the missing noun inferred from context.
rows.anchor: يقعقع خلف رجليه بشن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما الدهر إلا تارتان means one of the two turns brings death and the other a hard-won life; deletion after غير is comparable to omitting the rest of a compound name.
rows.anchor: أموت وأخرى أبتغى العيش أكدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When لا precedes an invocation noun already governed as a noun, it leaves the phrase in its prior nominal form; it need not be dualized.
rows.anchor: لا مرحبا ولا أهلا ولا كرامة ولا مسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا سلام عليك retains the phrase's form; Jarir's لا سلام على عمرو parallels the verbal prayer لا سلم الله عليه.
rows.anchor: لا سلام عليك لم تغير الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا بك السوء is a prayer meaning لا ساءك الله.
rows.anchor: ومثل لا سلام على عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا also joins expressions of wishing and gracious welcome, as it does their verbal equivalents such as لا أكرمك and لا أسرك.
rows.anchor: نحو كرامة ومسرة ونعمة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun construction is supported by the corresponding verbal construction: the imperative لا اضرب is not available, so the nominal form follows the preexisting noun pattern.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يجوز لا اضرب في الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا سواء is possible because لا substitutes for what سواء was predicated of; the same replacement explains لاها الله ذا.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أنك لا تقول هذان سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا نولك أن تفعل substitutes for لا ينبغي أن تفعل, so لا enters the construction as it enters ينبغي.
rows.anchor: أن تفعل لأنهم جعلوه معاقبا لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In بلا ذنب and similar phrases, لا with ب functions as one unit meaning without; بغير ذنب is the paraphrase when غير is not treated as an actual object.
rows.anchor: أجئتنا بغير شئ أي رائقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction لا شيء can diminish a matter, as in ما كان إلا كلا شيء and أنك ولا شيئا سواء.
rows.anchor: إلا كلا شئ وأنك ولا شيئا سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With حين لا حين, لا is treated as null; when لا براح or لا مستصرخ is accusative, that is the commoner construction, while nominative is also Arabic.
rows.anchor: والنصب أجود وأكثر من الرفع لأنك إذا قلت لا غلام فهي أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A predicate لا فارس is awkward unless paired with a contrasting description, because it answers an implied choice between فارس and شجاع.
rows.anchor: حتى تقول لا فارس ولا شجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet of Banū Sulūl uses the otherwise weak unpaired description لا نفع, showing the construction can occur in poetry.
rows.anchor: قال رجل من بني سلول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In questions, لا governs what follows just as in statements; Ḥassān's line supplies an example.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن لا في الاستفهام تعمل فيما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With interrogative alif and a wish meaning, ألا governs its complement like ordinary negative لا, dropping nunation and nun just as in the statement form.
rows.anchor: عملت فيما بعدها فنصبته ولا يحسن لها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reads ألا رجلا as a rhetorical prompt, not a wish: roughly ألا تروني رجلا جزاه الله خيرا.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل رحمه ~~الله عن قوله

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus explains the tanwīn in ألا رجلا as poetic necessity; Sibawayh says this is a possible analysis, while he presents al-Khalil's prompt reading for others.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فزعم أنه نون مضطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative wish construction is not nominative because it is neither an answer to a question nor a clause meaning ليس.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس بجواب لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ألا ماء ولبنا باردا حلوا, the adjectives are nunated because each describes a separate noun: cold water and sweet milk.
rows.anchor: لا يكون في الصفة إلا التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا غلام أفضل منك takes the accusative because it is a wish meaning اللهم هب لي غلاما and needs no predicate.
rows.anchor: إلا بالنصب لأنه دخل فيه معنى التمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ab and akh do not change in annexation even when used as personal names; naming does not alter أبوك and أخوك.
rows.anchor: أب وأخ ونحوهما تقول هذا أبوك وأخوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the proper name is فم, annexation gives فمك; فوك is not a restoration of a deleted mīm, but a form like ذو مال.
rows.anchor: فأما فم اسم رجل فإنك إذا أضفته قلت فمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man named ذو is annexed as ذواك, not ذوك, because ذو has no independent noun form when detached.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يكن له اسم مفرد ولكن تقول ذواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adverbs لدى, إلى, and على change to لداك, إلاك, and علاك when they become personal names.
rows.anchor: إذا صرن أسماء لرجال أو لنساء قلت هذا لداك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outside naming, لديك, عليك, and إليك preserve special forms that distinguish them from fully inflected nouns; proper names behave like ordinary nouns.
rows.anchor: كما فرقوا بين عني ومني وأخواتها وبين هني

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reports that some Arabs say علاك, لداك, and إلاك, with the other genitive enclitic pronouns behaving like kāf.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا الخليل أن ناسا من العرب يقولون علاك ولداك وإلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا may take forms such as كليهما by analogy with عليك and لديك in oblique contexts, since both constructions are commonly annexed adverbs.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل عمن قال رأيت كلا أخويك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy between كلا and على is based on frequent use and obligatory annexation; resemblance need not extend to every feature.
rows.anchor: لكثرتهما في كلامهم ولأنهما لا يخلوان من الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا is never singular; it always denotes a pair.
rows.anchor: ولا تفرد كلا إنما تكون للمثنى أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative clause after أيهم is acceptable when it contains هو; without هو, a form such as أيهم عاقل is judged awkward.
rows.anchor: فإذا أدخلت هو نصبت لأن الذي هو عاقل حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reports the rare construction ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا from an Arab speaker.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened construction with منطلق is rejected; the longer example is only a rare possibility, and few speakers use it.
rows.anchor: إذا طال الكلام فهو أمثل قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم may precede من and هل, but not interrogative alif, because أم is itself equivalent to the alif particle.
rows.anchor: تقول أم من تقول أم هل تقول ولا تقول أم أتقول وذاك لأن أم بمنزلة الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative أسماء such as أي, من, ما, and متى do not need alif: the question is already marked and the alif is omitted as redundant.
rows.anchor: من وما ومتى بمنزلة الألف وإنما هي أسماء بمنزلة هذا وذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم is needed to mark a shift from one alternative to another, while interrogative alif only initiates a question and is therefore omitted when redundant.
rows.anchor: منزلة لا بل للتحول من الشيء إلى الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine forms ending in two alifs, with the second represented by hamza, are diptote in both definite and indefinite use.
rows.anchor: إلا للتأنيث ولا تزادان أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza is a substitute for the second alif to avoid two adjacent vowelless letters, and behaves like the alif it replaces.
rows.anchor: الآخرة للتحريك لأنه لا ينجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine double alif is never added merely to lengthen a triliteral noun; the pattern is reserved for feminine marking.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أنك لم تر قط فعلاء مصروفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ʿalbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ the hamza replaces yāʾ, and alif plus yāʾ lengthens triliteral nouns; these are distinct from the feminine double-alif pattern.
rows.anchor: هذه الهمزة التي بعد الألف إنما هي بدل من ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs say قوباء as a masculine declinable form, assimilating it to فسطاط; its masculine use and declension support that analysis.
rows.anchor: من العرب من يقول هذا قوباء كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawghāʾ has two analyses: feminine like ʿawrāʾ and diptote, or masculine and declinable like qaḍqāḍ because its sounds are reduplicated.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة عوراء فيؤنث ولا يصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive of a three-letter feminine noun adds tāʾ to distinguish it from the masculine form.
rows.anchor: كل مؤنث كان على ثلاثة أحرف فتحقيره بالهاء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says tāʾ was added to mark femininity, but ʿanāq omits it because its length makes the extra marker heavy.
rows.anchor: أنهم إنما أدخلوا الهاء ليفرقوا بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A longer feminine such as samāʾ is shortened in the diminutive and then behaves like a three-letter noun, giving سميّة.
rows.anchor: في التحقير فيصير تحقيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman named Siqāʾ takes سقيقي without a feminine suffix because the proper name is already complete.
rows.anchor: حقرت امرأة اسمها سقاء قلت سقيقي ولم تدخلها الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports two diminutive analyses for ḥubārā: حبيرة preserves a feminine marker, while the other leaves the remaining form as four letters.
rows.anchor: قالوا في حبارى حبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A feminine word with the feminine alif in fifth position or later takes the diminutive pattern shown by لغيزى to لغيغيزة.
rows.anchor: قال في لغيزى لغيغيزة وفي جميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Half, when used as an adjective of a woman, remains masculine in the diminutive because it is a masculine adjective shared with feminine nouns; the same applies to رضى and خليق.
rows.anchor: تحقيرها نصيف وذاك لأنه مذكر وصف به مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh reports al-Khalil's account of the she-camel word الناب as masculine in the diminutive, نييب, because the masculine name became its established designation.
rows.anchor: عن الناب من الإبل فقال إنما قالوا نييب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman named حجر takes feminine حجيرة because حجر is a pure proper name, not a shared masculine adjective; a woman named فرس similarly takes فريسة.
rows.anchor: المرأة إذا سميت بحجر قلت حجيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh leaves the diminutive of a man's name عين or أذن without tāʾ; Yūnus adds tāʾ and cites أذينة, itself a diminutive name.
rows.anchor: ويونس يدخل الهاء ويحتج بأذينة وإنما سمي بمحقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Demonstratives keep their ordinary initial vowels in the diminutive, unlike other nouns, and add final alifs to distinguish their endings.
rows.anchor: على حالها قبل أن تحقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include هذا to هذيا, ذاك to ذياك, and ألا to أليا; the added alif gives them distinctive endings.
rows.anchor: ألحقوا هذه الألفات في أواخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive yāʾ in ذا is underlyingly third; one yāʾ is deleted when the sounds accumulate, and تيا is the diminutive of تا.
rows.anchor: اجتمعت الياءات وإنما حذفوها من ذبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms تماني and هاتا occur in poetry; Sibawayh cites Kaʿb al-Ghanawī and ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān.
rows.anchor: وخبر تماني أنما الموت في القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elongated أولاء becomes ألياء; feminine forms avoid the same diminutive pattern when it could cause confusion.
rows.anchor: وأما من مد أولاء فيقول ألياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronouns الذي and التي take diminutive forms اللذيا and اللتيا, supported by al-ʿAjjāj's line.
rows.anchor: الذي والتي تقول اللذيا واللتيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final alifs disappear in dual forms through frequent use; the text gives corresponding singular, plural, and dual forms for demonstratives and relatives.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثنيت حذفت هذه الألفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من and أي are not diminished when used as relative pronouns because they remain interrogative forms, while الذي is treated like a demonstrative.
rows.anchor: ولا يحقر من ولا أي إذا صارا بمنزلة الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اللاتي has no diminutive because اللتيات, the plural of اللتيا, supplies the needed form; Sibawayh compares this to using مسيان and عشيان instead of a diminutive of قصر.
rows.anchor: فلما استغنوا عنه صار مسقطا
